note: Operations on arrays and tensors, by their common framework-agnostic names (NumPy, PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow): shape, math, reductions, linear algebra

answers.q: Craft any view by lying about strides. NumPy's docs: "This function has to be used with extreme care."
Most of a transformer's FLOPs, and the reason GPUs grew tensor cores.
Same data, new shape. Complains only when the element counts disagree.
Free in theory: just swap the strides. Then the next op demands contiguous memory.
cat in PyTorch, concat in TensorFlow, concatenate in NumPy. One op, three names to typo.
Residual connections are just this. Arguably the most important op in deep learning.
The Hadamard product, for those who want to sound fancy.
One string, every contraction: 'bij,bjk->bik'. A 2018 blog post declared it all you need.
Reorder every axis at once. NCHW to NHWC and back again.
Where the convnet ends and the classifier begins.
Removes size-1 dims. Squeeze a batch of one and the batch dimension vanishes too.
Add a size-1 dim so broadcasting lines up. Also spelled None, newaxis and expand_dims.
Align shapes from the right, stretch the 1s. Elegant, until it silently does the wrong thing.
Concatenate's sibling: adds a new axis instead of growing an old one.
x[:, ::2] returns a view, so writing to it quietly edits the original.
Pick values along an axis with an index tensor. Every DQN's Q-value lookup.
Gather in reverse: write values to indexed slots. Duplicate indices? Some write wins.
Not differentiable, which is exactly why Gumbel-softmax exists.
The atom of attention: queries dot keys.
Column times row, rank one. Hebbian learning in a single op.
Branch without branching: pick from x or y elementwise by a condition.
In deep learning frameworks it's really cross-correlation. Nobody flips the kernel.
Subtract the max first or exp() overflows. Every framework quietly does it for you.
Numerical analysts beg you: call solve() instead of inv(). Faster and more stable.
Every matrix is a rotation, a stretch, and another rotation.
Cooley-Tukey 1965, though Gauss got there around 1805. O(n log n) ever since.
Copies the whole tensor k times. PyTorch calls this repeat; NumPy's repeat means something else.
Message passing in one line: sum each edge's message into its target node.
Set future positions to -inf before the softmax. The causal mask's favorite op.
Its output size depends on the data, which is why compilers hate it.
Shift elements cyclically. Swin Transformer's shifted windows are a torch.roll.
Everything above the diagonal is the future. Hello, causal mask.
einops: 'b c h w -> b (h w) c'. Reshapes you can actually read.
im2col: copy every sliding patch into a column and convolution becomes one big matmul.
Zero gradient almost everywhere. Quantization cheats with the straight-through estimator.
log Σ exp(x) without overflow: pull out the max first. The trick under every stable softmax.
Biased or unbiased? PyTorch divides by n-1 by default, NumPy by n.
Turn a mask into positions, or a PDF into a CDF, in one line.
Every entry of A times all of B. Shapes multiply; memory weeps.
Backprop through eigh and nearly equal eigenvalues will blow your gradients up.
The square root of a positive-definite matrix, at half the cost of LU. Gaussian processes run on it.
align_corners=True or False? The most argued-about boolean in computer vision.
Mathematically a one-hot matmul. Practically, just indexing a table.
Normalize, then dot. The heart of CLIP's contrastive loss.
Cut a tensor out of the autograd graph. The stop-gradient behind target networks and SimSiam.
Excludes the endpoint, unlike linspace. With float steps, the length may surprise you.
Two 1D ranges in, coordinate grids out. Remember indexing='ij', or suffer.
Sum gradients across every GPU and give everyone the result. Data parallelism in one call.
Copies a tensor into row-major order so .view() stops complaining.
a·b + c with a single rounding. GPU peak FLOP counts score each FMA as two.
The parallel prefix trick that lets linear RNNs like Mamba train fast on GPUs.
Differentiable bilinear sampling at arbitrary coordinates. The spatial transformer's engine.
The one op on this list that fuses a matmul, a softmax and another matmul into a single kernel.
